TextComparison.Note: Browser-based comparison hub for text, documents, URLs, XML, images, spreadsheets, presentations, and Markdown. Core compare tools are free; AI summaries require sign-in and an active subscription.
TextComparison.Title: Comparison Text | Compare Text, PDFs, URLs, XML, Word, Excel, Images, PPT, and Markdown
TextComparison.Short description(20-30 words): Comparison Text lets you compare text, PDFs, URLs, XML, Word, Excel, images, PPT, and Markdown online in one fast browser workspace.
TextComparison.Short Discription(100-150 words): Comparison Text is an online comparison hub built for quick side-by-side review across common content formats. Paste text, URLs, XML, or Markdown, or upload PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX files to inspect what changed between two versions. The workspace highlights added and removed content inline, shows left and right diff views, and provides summary stats for changed and unchanged characters. Text mode can ignore spaces, commas, tabs, and line breaks before diffing, while URL and XML modes normalize structured input for cleaner results. Core comparison tools are free to use, with optional AI summaries available for subscribed users who need a plain-language explanation of important changes.
TextComparison.Short Discription(150-250 words): Comparison Text is a focused online workspace for comparing text, documents, links, markup, images, spreadsheets, presentations, and Markdown without switching between separate tools. It supports raw text comparison, PDF text extraction, DOCX document review, XLSX and CSV spreadsheet comparison, URL query normalization, XML formatting, image metadata comparison, PPTX slide text extraction, and Markdown normalization. Each tool follows the same simple workflow: choose the right mode, add the original and revised versions, run the compare, then review inline highlights, side-by-side panes, and summary stats. Text compare includes delimiter controls so users can ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks when those differences are not meaningful. The first release is designed as a lightweight browser-based workspace, so core comparison tasks can be completed quickly without a required account. For users who need more context, Comparison Text also offers subscription-gated AI summaries that explain what changed, surface key differences, and suggest areas that deserve review. It is useful for copy edits, contracts, reports, spreadsheets, URLs, XML payloads, slide decks, Markdown files, and everyday version checks.
TextComparison.Long description (250-500 words):
Comparison Text is an online comparison hub for people who need to review changes across many everyday content formats from one consistent workspace. Instead of using one tool for text, another for PDFs, another for spreadsheets, and another for URLs, Comparison Text brings dedicated compare modes together under a single browser-based interface. Users can paste raw text, URLs, XML, or Markdown, or upload files such as PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.

The product is built around a simple three-step workflow: choose a tool, add the original and revised versions, and review the differences. Results include inline highlights, separate left and right views, and summary statistics for added, removed, unchanged, and total characters. Text Compare is useful for copy changes, prompts, snippets, templates, and plain-text files, with controls to ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks before diffing. PDF Compare and Word Compare focus on extracted text differences, making them practical for contracts, reports, drafts, and exported documents. Excel Compare handles XLSX and CSV content so users can spot changed rows or cell text faster. URL Compare normalizes query parameters to remove ordering noise, while XML Compare formats structured markup for clearer review. Markdown Compare supports pasted content or .md and .mdx uploads. Image Compare and PPT Compare add workflows for image files and PowerPoint presentations, including file-level checks and extracted slide text.

Core comparison tools are positioned as free and lightweight. Accounts are not required for the first-release core compare workflow, while AI-enhanced summaries are gated behind sign-in and an active subscription because they trigger billable AI usage. Paid plans provide credits for AI summaries and explanations, with monthly, annual, and one-time add-on options. Comparison Text is best for writers, marketers, developers, analysts, educators, operations teams, and anyone who regularly checks revisions before publishing, sharing, or approving content.

TextComparison.Feature description: Nine comparison modes: Text, PDF, URL, XML, Word DOCX, Excel/CSV, Image, PPTX, and Markdown. Features include paste or upload input, delimiter ignoring for text, URL query normalization, XML formatting, extracted text comparison for PDF/Word/PPT, spreadsheet text comparison, image metadata checks, inline highlights, side-by-side diff views, summary stats, related tool switching, and optional AI summaries for subscribed users.
TextComparison.Pricing: Core compare tools are free. AI-enhanced compare requires a subscription or add-on credits. One-time add-ons: AI Add-on 100 for $9, AI Add-on 200 for $16, AI Add-on 300 for $24. Monthly subscriptions: Starter $8/month, Pro $12/month, Scale $18/month. Annual subscriptions show effective monthly prices: Starter $6/month, Pro $9/month, Scale $14/month.

TextComparison.Subscription Model: Monthly and annual subscriptions for AI Compare Starter, AI Compare Pro, and AI Compare Scale. Subscriptions unlock AI-enhanced compare summaries and include credits.
TextComparison.Starting Price: $0 for core compare tools; paid AI plans start at $8/month monthly, $6/month effective annual price, or $9 for a one-time 100-credit add-on.
TextComparison.Promos: Project pricing includes crossed-out original prices and Stripe promotion-code mapping support, but no public promo code is specified.
TextComparison.Cost & Subscription: Free core comparison across all tools. Billable AI usage is subscription-gated. Monthly plans include 100, 200, or 300 credits valid for one month. Annual plans include 1,200, 2,400, or 3,600 credits valid for one year. One-time add-ons provide 100 credits valid 30 days, 200 credits valid 90 days, or 300 credits valid 365 days.
TextComparison.Credits System: Credits are used for AI-enhanced compare features such as AI result summaries and image compare explanations. Credit balances are shown in user navigation and settings. Admin tools can grant credits.
TextComparison.OS Compatibility: Web-based. Works on modern desktop and mobile operating systems through a browser, including Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and ChromeOS.
TextComparison.Platform Accessibility: Browser-based SaaS built with Next.js. Accessible through the web with responsive pages, light/dark theme support, English and Chinese locales, and no desktop installation required.
TextComparison.Offline Mode: Not positioned as an offline product. The compare workspace runs in the browser, but the site, authentication, payments, and AI summaries require network access.
TextComparison.Ease of Use: Simple three-step workflow: choose a comparison tool, paste or upload both versions, and review highlighted changes with inline view, left/right panes, and summary stats.
TextComparison.Payment Methods: Payment integrations present in the project: Stripe, PayPal, and Creem. Exact live methods depend on deployment configuration.
TextComparison.Media Support: Text, URL, XML, Markdown text, .md, .mdx, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, XLS, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.
TextComparison.Export Formats: No dedicated export or download format is specified in the current compare workspace. Results are displayed in-browser.
TextComparison.Data Storage Policy: Core compare workflows are described as running in the browser workspace in the first release. The privacy policy template covers account data, usage details, device information, cookies, and payment/billing data for signed-in or paid users.
TextComparison.User Anonvmitv: Core compare tools do not require an account in the first release, so anonymous use is supported for basic comparison. AI summaries require sign-in and an active subscription.

OldPhotoLive.Note: AI-powered old photo restoration service operated by Syndred Young. It restores damaged photos, colorizes black-and-white images, and creates animated video outputs from uploaded photos.
OldPhotoLive.Title: OldPhotoLive AI | AI Photo Restoration, Colorization, and Animation
OldPhotoLive.Short description(20-30 words): OldPhotoLive AI restores, colorizes, and animates old family photos online, turning faded memories into vivid images and short videos.
OldPhotoLive.Short Discription(100-150 words): OldPhotoLive AI is an online AI photo restoration tool for bringing old family photos back to life. Upload a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image, then let the service repair damage, remove scratches, improve clarity, add natural color, and create an animated video from the restored result. The workflow is designed around three simple steps: upload a photo, wait while AI restores, colorizes, and animates it, then download the final image or video. Free users can try one photo per day with limited resolution and watermarking, while paid users unlock higher-quality exports, watermark-free results, HD video, priority processing, and unlimited use on the Professional plan.
OldPhotoLive.Short Discription(150-250 words): OldPhotoLive AI is a web-based AI tool for restoring, colorizing, and animating old photos. It is built for people who want to improve faded family pictures, repair scratches or damage, recover facial details, add natural color to black-and-white images, and generate short animated videos from still photos. The product supports JPEG, PNG, and WebP uploads up to 10 MB and guides users through a clear flow: upload an image, let the AI process restoration, colorization, and animation, then review the before-and-after result and download the output. The free plan includes one photo per day, image export up to 800x600, 480p video output, and a watermark. Pay As You Go unlocks one credit, 2K image export up to 2048px, 720p HD video, and no watermark. The Professional subscription adds unlimited photos, 1080p premium video, no watermark, and priority processing. Users can sign in with Google, view processing history, retry failed jobs, and manage previous results. The service is useful for family memories, portraits, archival photos, and personal restoration projects.
OldPhotoLive.Long description (250-500 words):
OldPhotoLive AI is an AI-powered photo restoration, colorization, and animation service for people who want to revive old family photos online. The product focuses on a practical restoration workflow rather than a generic image editor: users upload an old or damaged photo, the system improves the image with AI restoration, adds natural color when appropriate, and can generate an animated video output from the still image. It is especially suited for portraits, family photos, landscape memories, faded prints, scratched images, and black-and-white photos that need a more vivid modern version.

The core user flow is simple. A user uploads a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image up to 10 MB, waits while the pipeline moves through upload, restore, colorize, and animate stages, then reviews the before-and-after comparison and downloads the restored image or animated video. The interface includes progress states, retry behavior for failed jobs, processing history, and download actions for image and video results. The site copy positions most jobs as completing within one to three minutes, with complex restorations or animations sometimes taking longer.

OldPhotoLive AI uses a freemium pricing model. The free plan lets users try one photo per day, with image export up to 800x600, 480p video output, and a watermark. The Pay As You Go option costs $0.99 for one credit and enables 2K image export up to 2048px, 720p HD video, and no watermark. The Professional plan costs $19.99 per month and includes unlimited photos, 2K image export, 1080p premium video, no watermark, and priority processing. Payments are handled through Stripe, and Google sign-in is used for account access.

The privacy and legal pages describe cloud storage for uploaded and generated media, task history access, account information from Google sign-in, Stripe billing metadata, analytics, logs, and operational providers for authentication, payments, storage, queueing, compute, email, and analytics. OldPhotoLive AI is operated by Syndred Young and targets users who want a direct way to restore and animate personal photo memories without installing desktop software.

GraffitiName.Title: Graffiti Name Generator for creating graffiti names, tag ideas, and downloadable name art
GraffitiName.Short description(20-30 words): Graffiti Name AI helps you create graffiti names, test tag styles, and download finished PNG name art from one homepage generator.
GraffitiName.Short Discription(100-150 words): Graffiti Name AI is an online graffiti name generator for creating tag ideas, bubble letters, throw-up styles, marker looks, street block lettering, and wildstyle-lite name art. Users type a name, compare curated style directions, switch scenes such as wall poster, sticker sheet, or mural concept, and generate finished artwork directly from the homepage. Browsing examples is public, while sign-in is required before generating and downloading. The product uses a credits-backed model: monthly and yearly memberships include recurring credits, and a small one-time credit pack is available for occasional renders. Completed output can be downloaded as PNG artwork, making the tool useful for name exploration, visual inspiration, social graphics, and quick graffiti-style design tests.
GraffitiName.Short Discription(150-250 words): Graffiti Name AI is a web-based graffiti name generator built around a fast homepage workflow. Instead of sending users through multiple pages, the product lets them type a name, preview visual directions, choose styles, switch scenes, generate AI artwork, and download the finished result in one place. The generator currently covers tag, bubble, throw-up, street block, marker, and wildstyle-lite directions, with curated examples that help users judge style quality before spending credits. Scene options include graffiti wall poster, sticker sheet, and mural concept looks, so the same name can be tested across different creative contexts. Browsing examples and reading guides are public, but users must sign in before generating or downloading artwork. Pricing is simple: a $9.99 monthly membership includes 120 credits every month, a $99.99 yearly membership includes 1,440 credits every year, and a $4.99 one-time pack includes 50 credits. The project includes downloadable PNG output, visible generation progress, credit balance handling, and support content around graffiti names, tagger names, name availability, and how to write a name in graffiti. It is useful for creators, hobbyists, designers, and anyone exploring readable street-style name art.
GraffitiName.Long description (250-500 words):
Graffiti Name AI is an online graffiti name generator designed to help users move from a first name idea to finished downloadable name art without leaving the homepage. The product focuses on names, tags, and lettering directions rather than generic image generation. Users can type a name, test style directions, browse curated examples, choose a scene, generate the artwork, and download the completed image once it is ready. The homepage copy emphasizes that short names with three to ten letters usually create the strongest graffiti compositions.

The generator supports several graffiti-inspired directions, including tag, bubble, throw-up, street block, marker, and wildstyle-lite. It also includes scene choices such as wall poster, sticker sheet, and mural concept, allowing the same name to be explored in different formats. Curated examples like bubble, marker, street block, tag, throw-up, and wildstyle-lite previews help users pick a direction before they spend credits. The result is presented as finished downloadable artwork rather than a vague preview, and the interface shows visible generation states so users know when rendering is waiting, running, or complete.

Graffiti Name AI uses a freemium discovery model with paid generation. Browsing examples and product content is public, but sign-in is required before generating or downloading artwork. AI generation uses credits. The monthly membership costs $9.99 and includes 120 credits every month, full generator access, and PNG downloads. The yearly membership costs $99.99 and includes 1,440 credits every year, a lower effective cost than monthly, full generator access, and PNG downloads. A one-time 50-credit pack costs $4.99 and is aimed at occasional renders and quick experiments.

The privacy and terms pages state that the service may process generator input such as names, letters, and style choices, plus technical usage data and optional email communication. If AI enhancement is enabled, selected prompts and style parameters may be sent to third-party model providers such as Replicate. Outputs are automatically generated and are not guaranteed to be exclusive, commercially cleared, trademark-safe, or non-infringing, so users are responsible for reviewing results before public or commercial use.

The product focuses on a practical restoration workflow rather than a generic image editor: users upload an old or damaged photo, the system improves the image with AI restoration, adds natural color when appropriate, and can generate an animated video output from the still image. It is especially suited for portraits, family photos, landscape memories, faded prints, scratched images, and black-and-white photos that need a more vivid modern version.

The core user flow is simple. A user uploads a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image up to 10 MB, waits while the pipeline moves through upload, restore, colorize, and animate stages, then reviews the before-and-after comparison and downloads the restored image or animated video. The interface includes progress states, retry behavior for failed jobs, processing history, and download actions for image and video results. The site copy positions most jobs as completing within one to three minutes, with complex restorations or animations sometimes taking longer.

OldPhotoLive AI uses a freemium pricing model. The free plan lets users try one photo per day, with image export up to 800x600, 480p video output, and a watermark. The Pay As You Go option costs $0.99 for one credit and enables 2K image export up to 2048px, 720p HD video, and no watermark. The Professional plan costs $19.99 per month and includes unlimited photos, 2K image export, 1080p premium video, no watermark, and priority processing. Payments are handled through Stripe, and Google sign-in is used for account access.

The privacy and legal pages describe cloud storage for uploaded and generated media, task history access, account information from Google sign-in, Stripe billing metadata, analytics, logs, and operational providers for authentication, payments, storage, queueing, compute, email, and analytics. OldPhotoLive AI is operated by Syndred Young and targets users who want a direct way to restore and animate personal photo memories without installing desktop software.

config.anchorText: Comparison Text | Compare Text, PDFs, URLs, XML, Word, Excel, Images, PPT, and Markdown
config.commentTemplate:
Comparison Text is an online comparison hub for people who need to review changes across many everyday content formats from one consistent workspace. Instead of using one tool for text, another for PDFs, another for spreadsheets, and another for URLs, Comparison Text brings dedicated compare modes together under a single browser-based interface. Users can paste raw text, URLs, XML, or Markdown, or upload files such as PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.

The product is built around a simple three-step workflow: choose a tool, add the original and revised versions, and review the differences. Results include inline highlights, separate left and right views, and summary statistics for added, removed, unchanged, and total characters. Text Compare is useful for copy changes, prompts, snippets, templates, and plain-text files, with controls to ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks before diffing. PDF Compare and Word Compare focus on extracted text differences, making them practical for contracts, reports, drafts, and exported documents. Excel Compare handles XLSX and CSV content so users can spot changed rows or cell text faster. URL Compare normalizes query parameters to remove ordering noise, while XML Compare formats structured markup for clearer review. Markdown Compare supports pasted content or .md and .mdx uploads. Image Compare and PPT Compare add workflows for image files and PowerPoint presentations, including file-level checks and extracted slide text.

Core comparison tools are positioned as free and lightweight. Accounts are not required for the first-release core compare workflow, while AI-enhanced summaries are gated behind sign-in and an active subscription because they trigger billable AI usage. Paid plans provide credits for AI summaries and explanations, with monthly, annual, and one-time add-on options. Comparison Text is best for writers, marketers, developers, analysts, educators, operations teams, and anyone who regularly checks revisions before publishing, sharing, or approving content.

config.commentTemplate:
Graffiti Name AI is an online graffiti name generator designed to help users move from a first name idea to finished downloadable name art without leaving the homepage. The product focuses on names, tags, and lettering directions rather than generic image generation. Users can type a name, test style directions, browse curated examples, choose a scene, generate the artwork, and download the completed image once it is ready. The homepage copy emphasizes that short names with three to ten letters usually create the strongest graffiti compositions.

The generator supports several graffiti-inspired directions, including tag, bubble, throw-up, street block, marker, and wildstyle-lite. It also includes scene choices such as wall poster, sticker sheet, and mural concept, allowing the same name to be explored in different formats. Curated examples like bubble, marker, street block, tag, throw-up, and wildstyle-lite previews help users pick a direction before they spend credits. The result is presented as finished downloadable artwork rather than a vague preview, and the interface shows visible generation states so users know when rendering is waiting, running, or complete.

Graffiti Name AI uses a freemium discovery model with paid generation. Browsing examples and product content is public, but sign-in is required before generating or downloading artwork. AI generation uses credits. The monthly membership costs $9.99 and includes 120 credits every month, full generator access, and PNG downloads. The yearly membership costs $99.99 and includes 1,440 credits every year, a lower effective cost than monthly, full generator access, and PNG downloads. A one-time 50-credit pack costs $4.99 and is aimed at occasional renders and quick experiments.

The privacy and terms pages state that the service may process generator input such as names, letters, and style choices, plus technical usage data and optional email communication. If AI enhancement is enabled, selected prompts and style parameters may be sent to third-party model providers such as Replicate. Outputs are automatically generated and are not guaranteed to be exclusive, commercially cleared, trademark-safe, or non-infringing, so users are responsible for reviewing results before public or commercial use.

Users can paste raw text, URLs, XML, or Markdown, or upload files such as PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.

The product is built around a simple three-step workflow: choose a tool, add the original and revised versions, and review the differences. Results include inline highlights, separate left and right views, and summary statistics for added, removed, unchanged, and total characters. Text Compare is useful for copy changes, prompts, snippets, templates, and plain-text files, with controls to ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks before diffing. PDF Compare and Word Compare focus on extracted text differences, making them practical for contracts, reports, drafts, and exported documents. Excel Compare handles XLSX and CSV content so users can spot changed rows or cell text faster. The workspace highlights added and removed content inline, shows left and right diff views, and provides summary stats for changed and unchanged characters. Text mode can ignore spaces, commas, tabs, and line breaks before diffing, while URL and XML modes normalize structured input for cleaner results. Core comparison tools are free to use, with optional AI summaries available for subscribed users who need a plain-language explanation of important changes.
projectFields.Short Discription(150-250 words): Comparison Text is a focused online workspace for comparing text, documents, links, markup, images, spreadsheets, presentations, and Markdown without switching between separate tools. It supports raw text comparison, PDF text extraction, DOCX document review, XLSX and CSV spreadsheet comparison, URL query normalization, XML formatting, image metadata comparison, PPTX slide text extraction, and Markdown normalization. Each tool follows the same simple workflow: choose the right mode, add the original and revised versions, run the compare, then review inline highlights, side-by-side panes, and summary stats. Text compare includes delimiter controls so users can ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks when those differences are not meaningful. The first release is designed as a lightweight browser-based workspace, so core comparison tasks can be completed quickly without a required account. For users who need more context, Comparison Text also offers subscription-gated AI summaries that explain what changed, surface key differences, and suggest areas that deserve review. It is useful for copy edits, contracts, reports, spreadsheets, URLs, XML payloads, slide decks, Markdown files, and everyday version checks.
projectFields.Long description (250-500 words):
Comparison Text is an online comparison hub for people who need to review changes across many everyday content formats from one consistent workspace. Instead of using one tool for text, another for PDFs, another for spreadsheets, and another for URLs, Comparison Text brings dedicated compare modes together under a single browser-based interface. Users can paste raw text, URLs, XML, or Markdown, or upload files such as PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.

The product is built around a simple three-step workflow: choose a tool, add the original and revised versions, and review the differences. Results include inline highlights, separate left and right views, and summary statistics for added, removed, unchanged, and total characters. Text Compare is useful for copy changes, prompts, snippets, templates, and plain-text files, with controls to ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks before diffing. PDF Compare and Word Compare focus on extracted text differences, making them practical for contracts, reports, drafts, and exported documents. Excel Compare handles XLSX and CSV content so users can spot changed rows or cell text faster. URL Compare normalizes query parameters to remove ordering noise, while XML Compare formats structured markup for clearer review. Markdown Compare supports pasted content or .md and .mdx uploads. Image Compare and PPT Compare add workflows for image files and PowerPoint presentations, including file-level checks and extracted slide text.

Core comparison tools are positioned as free and lightweight. Accounts are not required for the first-release core compare workflow, while AI-enhanced summaries are gated behind sign-in and an active subscription because they trigger billable AI usage. Paid plans provide credits for AI summaries and explanations, with monthly, annual, and one-time add-on options. Comparison Text is best for writers, marketers, developers, analysts, educators, operations teams, and anyone who regularly checks revisions before publishing, sharing, or approving content.

projectFields.Promos: Project pricing includes crossed-out original prices and Stripe promotion-code mapping support, but no public promo code is specified.
projectFields.Cost & Subscription: Free core comparison across all tools. Billable AI usage is subscription-gated. Monthly plans include 100, 200, or 300 credits valid for one month. Annual plans include 1,200, 2,400, or 3,600 credits valid for one year. One-time add-ons provide 100 credits valid 30 days, 200 credits valid 90 days, or 300 credits valid 365 days.
projectFields.Credits System: Credits are used for AI-enhanced compare features such as AI result summaries and image compare explanations. Credit balances are shown in user navigation and settings. Admin tools can grant credits.
projectFields.OS Compatibility: Web-based. Works on modern desktop and mobile operating systems through a browser, including Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and ChromeOS.
projectFields.Platform Accessibility: Browser-based SaaS built with Next.js. Accessible through the web with responsive pages, light/dark theme support, English and Chinese locales, and no desktop installation required.
projectFields.Offline Mode: Not positioned as an offline product. The compare workspace runs in the browser, but the site, authentication, payments, and AI summaries require network access.
projectFields.Ease of Use: Simple three-step workflow: choose a comparison tool, paste or upload both versions, and review highlighted changes with inline view, left/right panes, and summary stats.
projectFields.Payment Methods: Payment integrations present in the project: Stripe, PayPal, and Creem. Exact live methods depend on deployment configuration.
projectFields.Media Support: Text, URL, XML, Markdown text, .md, .mdx, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, XLS, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.
projectFields.Export Formats: No dedicated export or download format is specified in the current compare workspace. Results are displayed in-browser.
projectFields.Data Storage Policy: Core compare workflows are described as running in the browser workspace in the first release. The privacy policy template covers account data, usage details, device information, cookies, and payment/billing data for signed-in or paid users.
projectFields.User Anonvmitv: Core compare tools do not require an account in the first release, so anonymous use is supported for basic comparison. AI summaries require sign-in and an active subscription.

projectFields.Long description (250-500 words):
Comparison Text is an online comparison hub for people who need to review changes across many everyday content formats from one consistent workspace. Instead of using one tool for text, another for PDFs, another for spreadsheets, and another for URLs, Comparison Text brings dedicated compare modes together under a single browser-based interface. Users can paste raw text, URLs, XML, or Markdown, or upload files such as PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.

The product is built around a simple three-step workflow: choose a tool, add the original and revised versions, and review the differences. Results include inline highlights, separate left and right views, and summary statistics for added, removed, unchanged, and total characters. Text Compare is useful for copy changes, prompts, snippets, templates, and plain-text files, with controls to ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks before diffing. PDF Compare and Word Compare focus on extracted text differences, making them practical for contracts, reports, drafts, and exported documents. Excel Compare handles XLSX and CSV content so users can spot changed rows or cell text faster. URL Compare normalizes query parameters to remove ordering noise, while XML Compare formats structured markup for clearer review. Markdown Compare supports pasted content or .md and .mdx uploads. Image Compare and PPT Compare add workflows for image files and PowerPoint presentations, including file-level checks and extracted slide text.

Core comparison tools are positioned as free and lightweight. Accounts are not required for the first-release core compare workflow, while AI-enhanced summaries are gated behind sign-in and an active subscription because they trigger billable AI usage. Paid plans provide credits for AI summaries and explanations, with monthly, annual, and one-time add-on options. Comparison Text is best for writers, marketers, developers, analysts, educators, operations teams, and anyone who regularly checks revisions before publishing, sharing, or approving content.

Users can paste raw text, URLs, XML, or Markdown, or upload files such as PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.

The product is built around a simple three-step workflow: choose a tool, add the original and revised versions, and review the differences. Results include inline highlights, separate left and right views, and summary statistics for added, removed, unchanged, and total characters. Text Compare is useful for copy changes, prompts, snippets, templates, and plain-text files, with controls to ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks before diffing. PDF Compare and Word Compare focus on extracted text differences, making them practical for contracts, reports, drafts, and exported documents. Excel Compare handles XLSX and CSV content so users can spot changed rows or cell text faster. Core comparison tools are positioned as free and lightweight. projectFields.Short description(20-30 words): Comparison Text lets you compare text, PDFs, URLs, XML, Word, Excel, images, PPT, and Markdown online in one fast browser workspace.
projectFields.Short Discription(100-150 words): Comparison Text is an online comparison hub built for quick side-by-side review across common content formats. Paste text, URLs, XML, or Markdown, or upload PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX files to inspect what changed between two versions. The workspace highlights added and removed content inline, shows left and right diff views, and provides summary stats for changed and unchanged characters. Text mode can ignore spaces, commas, tabs, and line breaks before diffing, while URL and XML modes normalize structured input for cleaner results. Core comparison tools are free to use, with optional AI summaries available for subscribed users who need a plain-language explanation of important changes.
projectFields.Short Discription(150-250 words): Comparison Text is a focused online workspace for comparing text, documents, links, markup, images, spreadsheets, presentations, and Markdown without switching between separate tools. It supports raw text comparison, PDF text extraction, DOCX document review, XLSX and CSV spreadsheet comparison, URL query normalization, XML formatting, image metadata comparison, PPTX slide text extraction, and Markdown normalization. Each tool follows the same simple workflow: choose the right mode, add the original and revised versions, run the compare, then review inline highlights, side-by-side panes, and summary stats. Text compare includes delimiter controls so users can ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks when those differences are not meaningful. The first release is designed as a lightweight browser-based workspace, so core comparison tasks can be completed quickly without a required account. For users who need more context, Comparison Text also offers subscription-gated AI summaries that explain what changed, surface key differences, and suggest areas that deserve review. It is useful for copy edits, contracts, reports, spreadsheets, URLs, XML payloads, slide decks, Markdown files, and everyday version checks.
projectFields.Long description (250-500 words):
Comparison Text is an online comparison hub for people who need to review changes across many everyday content formats from one consistent workspace. Instead of using one tool for text, another for PDFs, another for spreadsheets, and another for URLs, Comparison Text brings dedicated compare modes together under a single browser-based interface. Users can paste raw text, URLs, XML, or Markdown, or upload files such as PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.

The product is built around a simple three-step workflow: choose a tool, add the original and revised versions, and review the differences. Results include inline highlights, separate left and right views, and summary statistics for added, removed, unchanged, and total characters. Text Compare is useful for copy changes, prompts, snippets, templates, and plain-text files, with controls to ignore spaces, commas, tabs, or line breaks before diffing. PDF Compare and Word Compare focus on extracted text differences, making them practical for contracts, reports, drafts, and exported documents. Excel Compare handles XLSX and CSV content so users can spot changed rows or cell text faster. URL Compare normalizes query parameters to remove ordering noise, while XML Compare formats structured markup for clearer review. Markdown Compare supports pasted content or .md and .mdx uploads. Image Compare and PPT Compare add workflows for image files and PowerPoint presentations, including file-level checks and extracted slide text.

Core comparison tools are positioned as free and lightweight. Accounts are not required for the first-release core compare workflow, while AI-enhanced summaries are gated behind sign-in and an active subscription because they trigger billable AI usage. Paid plans provide credits for AI summaries and explanations, with monthly, annual, and one-time add-on options. Comparison Text is best for writers, marketers, developers, analysts, educators, operations teams, and anyone who regularly checks revisions before publishing, sharing, or approving content.

projectFields.Feature description: Nine comparison modes: Text, PDF, URL, XML, Word DOCX, Excel/CSV, Image, PPTX, and Markdown. Features include paste or upload input, delimiter ignoring for text, URL query normalization, XML formatting, extracted text comparison for PDF/Word/PPT, spreadsheet text comparison, image metadata checks, inline highlights, side-by-side diff views, summary stats, related tool switching, and optional AI summaries for subscribed users.
projectFields.Pricing: Core compare tools are free. AI-enhanced compare requires a subscription or add-on credits. One-time add-ons: AI Add-on 100 for $9, AI Add-on 200 for $16, AI Add-on 300 for $24. Monthly subscriptions: Starter $8/month, Pro $12/month, Scale $18/month. Annual subscriptions show effective monthly prices: Starter $6/month, Pro $9/month, Scale $14/month.
projectFields.PRICING TYPE: Freemium with paid AI-enhanced features, subscription plans, and one-time credit add-ons.
projectFields.Subscription Model: Monthly and annual subscriptions for AI Compare Starter, AI Compare Pro, and AI Compare Scale. Subscriptions unlock AI-enhanced compare summaries and include credits.
projectFields.Starting Price: $0 for core compare tools; paid AI plans start at $8/month monthly, $6/month effective annual price, or $9 for a one-time 100-credit add-on.
projectFields.Promos: Project pricing includes crossed-out original prices and Stripe promotion-code mapping support, but no public promo code is specified.
projectFields.Cost & Subscription: Free core comparison across all tools. Billable AI usage is subscription-gated. Monthly plans include 100, 200, or 300 credits valid for one month. Annual plans include 1,200, 2,400, or 3,600 credits valid for one year. One-time add-ons provide 100 credits valid 30 days, 200 credits valid 90 days, or 300 credits valid 365 days.
projectFields.Credits System: Credits are used for AI-enhanced compare features such as AI result summaries and image compare explanations. Credit balances are shown in user navigation and settings. Admin tools can grant credits.
projectFields.OS Compatibility: Web-based. Works on modern desktop and mobile operating systems through a browser, including Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and ChromeOS.
projectFields.Platform Accessibility: Browser-based SaaS built with Next.js. Accessible through the web with responsive pages, light/dark theme support, English and Chinese locales, and no desktop installation required.
projectFields.Offline Mode: Not positioned as an offline product. The compare workspace runs in the browser, but the site, authentication, payments, and AI summaries require network access.
projectFields.Ease of Use: Simple three-step workflow: choose a comparison tool, paste or upload both versions, and review highlighted changes with inline view, left/right panes, and summary stats.
projectFields.Payment Methods: Payment integrations present in the project: Stripe, PayPal, and Creem. Exact live methods depend on deployment configuration.
projectFields.Media Support: Text, URL, XML, Markdown text, .md, .mdx, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, XLS, CSV, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and PPTX.
projectFields.Export Formats: No dedicated export or download format is specified in the current compare workspace. Results are displayed in-browser.
projectFields.Data Storage Policy: Core compare workflows are described as running in the browser workspace in the first release. The privacy policy template covers account data, usage details, device information, cookies, and payment/billing data for signed-in or paid users.
projectFields.User Anonvmitv: Core compare tools do not require an account in the first release, so anonymous use is supported for basic comparison. AI summaries require sign-in and an active subscription.
